title: K-th Smallest in Lexicographical Order
summary: Given two integers n and k , return the k-th lexicographically smallest integer within the range from 1 to n .
statement: Given two integers n and k , return the k-th lexicographically smallest integer within the range from 1 to n .
constraints: 1 <= k <= n <= 10^9. Rank the integers 1 through n by their decimal text, without leading zeros.
k is one-based. Return the selected integer, not its position or the whole sorted list.
hints: Decimal prefixes form a tree whose preorder is lexicographic order.
Count integers under the current prefix to choose between skipping that subtree and descending into it.
At each digit length intersect [prefix*10^d,(prefix+1)*10^d) with [1,n+1); sum widths and compare with remaining rank.
Skip a subtree when its count fits before the target; otherwise consume its root and descend. Counting levels avoids enumerating up to a billion values.
editorial: A prefix subtree contains consecutive numeric intervals at successive decimal lengths. Clip each interval at n+1 to count it exactly. Starting at prefix 1 and rank offset k-1, skip whole subtrees or descend to the first child. At most a fixed number of sibling moves occur at each digit level, each requiring a logarithmic-depth count. This yields O(log^2 n) time and O(1) space.

tests.explanation: The order starts 1,10,11,12,13,2,…, so rank 2 contains 10.
After all five numbers beginning with 1, rank 6 contains 2. A whole prefix subtree can be skipped.
